- Délai OSC 11 : 500 ms ; theme_light par défaut : github-light
- Q1 : embarquer themes/*.json via go:embed (fichier utilisateur prioritaire)
- Q2 : tout échec de chargement de thème → défaut + Warn ; test existant TestASavedThemeWithAnInvalidHex... réécrit
- Q3/Q4 (prudents, architect) : contrôle contraste ≥4,5:1 à l'exécution pour thèmes perso ; deux champs cycle dans :config
- pm et wiki-scout sautés

## Points ouverts
- Plan à valider ; R2 (auto choisi en session sans cache : reset OSC 111 puis requête 100 ms)
- Hors périmètre : changement de contexte ne réapplique pas le thème (story séparée)

Après validation : tester (rouge étape 1) puis coder.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/skills/git-worktree-pr

## Work starts in a new worktree

**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
the current `main`, **under `.worktrees/` inside the repository**:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main
cd .worktrees/<branch>
```

Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
Editing does.

**Under the repository, not beside it.** This reverses what this file said until
now, and the reason it gave was wrong. It claimed a worktree at `.worktrees/x`
would be compiled by `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`. It would not: the go
tool skips every directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`, so `.worktrees/`
is invisible to `./...`. Verified rather than assumed — a package of deliberately
invalid Go placed under `.worktrees/` builds clean and `go list ./...` does not
name it. The old argument holds for `worktrees/` without the dot, which is
presumably where it came from.

What decides it is the **sandbox mount**, and it cost a full debugging session to
find. A direct-mode sandbox mounts *this directory only*. A sibling worktree at
`../devdesk-<branch>` is therefore outside the mount, so its **files** are written
into the container's private layer and never reach the host — while `.git` is
inside the mount and stays shared. Refs agree, files diverge, and nothing warns:
the branch tip moves, the host's copy of those files does not, and `git status`
on the host reports the *stale* content as uncommitted modifications. An agent
and the person testing its work end up compiling different code while both
believe they are on the same branch. Under `.worktrees/`, host and sandbox see
one filesystem.

Two effects worth knowing, neither blocking:

- `.worktrees/` is in `.gitignore`; a worktree there is not a change to the tree.
- Claude Code discovers the nested `.claude/` of each worktree, so its skills and
  rules appear a second time, prefixed by the worktree path. Harmless, and the
  price of the directory being inside the repo.

**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:

| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `~/.devdesk/` — contexts, `config.yaml`, scan caches | two agents editing settings or scanning at once overwrite each other's; nothing warns |
| the host keyring, Docker, the ports the app binds | one at a time, whoever gets there first |
| `.git/hooks` | verified: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the **main** checkout's, so the Entire checkpoint and pre-push hooks fire normally from a worktree |
| `origin` | inherited — `git push -u origin <branch>` goes through the mirror as usual |

`mise` tasks and `go build` work unchanged; both read the tree they are run in.

**`entire graph` indexes per directory.** A fresh worktree has no index, so the
first `entire graph search` there pays a full build (~5 s on this repo, measured)
and the symbol ids it returns are namespaced by the directory name
(`local/<branch>:Go:…`). Nothing breaks; do not be surprised by the first search
being slow or by ids that do not match another worktree's.

**Clean up when the PR is merged**, from the main checkout:

```bash
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
git worktree list          # what is still out there
git worktree prune         # after a directory was deleted by hand
```

`git worktree remove` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, which is the
point — look before forcing.

**The main checkout stays on `main` and stays clean.** It is what `git fetch
origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` needs after each merge, and what
every new worktree is cut from.

## Git workflow — pull requests only

**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:

```
! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
```

This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.

**The repository is public since 2026-09-06**, which is what makes GitHub-side
enforcement possible at all: a private repo on a free personal plan answers
`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` on both
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` — that was the prior state, and it is not a
description to trust going forward if the repo ever goes private again. Do not
cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting `"protected":
false` as proof of anything either way: that field only ever reflects legacy
branch protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and it read `false`
on the free-private plan whatever the configuration. Query
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` itself (or `gh ruleset check main`) for the
real answer.

A ruleset named `main-protection` (id `22399372`) now targets `refs/heads/main`
only — deliberately not `entire/checkpoints/v1`, which receives automatic
pushes from the Entire hook and would break if rule-gated. It requires a pull
request (0 approving reviews — solo maintainer, the PR is a record not a review
gate) with the `Lint and build` and `Test` checks from `ci.yml` passing,
blocks force-pushes and branch deletion, and grants no bypass. This closes the
gap the mirror alone left open: the Entire mirror's rejection of a direct push
to `main` was, until now, the *only* protection — a second remote pointing
straight at GitHub would have sailed through (see the warning against adding
one, below). Now GitHub itself refuses that push too.

**The `Entire Gates` check is expected to stay red on this repository.** It is
a PR check from the `entire` app, and its **Approvals** gate fails until another
reviewer approves the trail. That approval cannot arrive: the repository has one
developer, so the gate cannot be green, and no second account or dummy reviewer
should be added to satisfy it. The check is not required by `main-protection`
(GitHub reports the PR as `UNSTABLE` but `MERGEABLE`), so a red `Entire Gates`
alone does not block a merge. Merge once `Lint and build` and `Test` pass. The
Findings, Checks and Up to date gates must stay green: if any of them fails, it
is a real signal, so stop and raise it with the user. Agents (orchestrator,
devops) must not stop to ask for agreement over the Approvals failure alone.
To read the reason:
`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="Entire Gates") | .output.summary'`.

Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
and is forwarded to GitHub.

**Pull requests are GitHub's, not Entire's.** Entire has no merge-request
concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So
the PR steps below are `gh`, and the branch they review is one `origin` carried
to GitHub. `entire review` (labs) runs a multi-agent review against the current
branch and is a pre-merge step, not a substitute for the PR.

```bash
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main   # work happens here
git push -u origin <branch>                     # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch>
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
# then, from the main checkout:
git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see below
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
```

**`-R anthnel/devdesk` is not optional.** `gh` infers the repository from a
remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this
repository point to a known GitHub host"*. The flag names the repo directly.
Do not solve this by adding a GitHub remote — see below.

**After a merge, `origin` can read stale for a minute or two.** The mirror lags
GitHub, so `git fetch origin` right after `gh pr merge` may return the *previous*
`main` — with no error, which is the part that misleads. `gh pr view <n> --json state`
says `MERGED` while `git rev-parse origin/main` still points at the commit before
it. Re-run the fetch a moment later; `gh` is what to trust in the meantime,
because it talks to GitHub directly and needs no remote.

**Do not add a second remote pointing at GitHub to work around that.** The
`main-protection` ruleset (above) would now refuse a direct `git push github
main` too, so it is no longer the *only* defeat of the only protection — but a
direct push still bypasses the mirror, and with it the Entire hook that
records checkpoints and sessions, which is not visible until much later.
`origin` is the only remote, deliberately.

**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.


**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
clean:

```bash
git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> .worktrees/<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
cd .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
git reset --hard origin/main
git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
git worktree remove .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
```

### Remotes

| Remote | URL | Use |
|--------|-----|-----|
| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — everything: clone, fetch, push |

**There is one remote, and there should stay one.** The repository is hosted on

## Work starts in a new worktree

**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
the current `main`, **under `.worktrees/` inside the repository**:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main
cd .worktrees/<branch>
```

Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
Editing does.

**Under the repository, not beside it.** This reverses what this file said until
now, and the reason it gave was wrong. It claimed a worktree at `.worktrees/x`
would be compiled by `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`. It would not: the go
tool skips every directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`, so `.worktrees/`
is invisible to `./...`. Verified rather than assumed — a package of deliberately
invalid Go placed under `.worktrees/` builds clean and `go list ./...` does not
name it. The old argument holds for `worktrees/` without the dot, which is
presumably where it came from.

What decides it is the **sandbox mount**, and it cost a full debugging session to
find. A direct-mode sandbox mounts *this directory only*. A sibling worktree at
`../devdesk-<branch>` is therefore outside the mount, so its **files** are written
into the container's private layer and never reach the host — while `.git` is
inside the mount and stays shared. Refs agree, files diverge, and nothing warns:
the branch tip moves, the host's copy of those files does not, and `git status`
on the host reports the *stale* content as uncommitted modifications. An agent
and the person testing its work end up compiling different code while both
believe they are on the same branch. Under `.worktrees/`, host and sandbox see
one filesystem.

Two effects worth knowing, neither blocking:

- `.worktrees/` is in `.gitignore`; a worktree there is not a change to the tree.
- Claude Code discovers the nested `.claude/` of each worktree, so its skills and
  rules appear a second time, prefixed by the worktree path. Harmless, and the
  price of the directory being inside the repo.

**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:

| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `~/.devdesk/` — contexts, `config.yaml`, scan caches | two agents editing settings or scanning at once overwrite each other's; nothing warns |
| the host keyring, Docker, the ports the app binds | one at a time, whoever gets there first |
| `.git/hooks` | verified: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the **main** checkout's, so the Entire checkpoint and pre-push hooks fire normally from a worktree |
| `origin` | inherited — `git push -u origin <branch>` goes through the mirror as usual |

`mise` tasks and `go build` work unchanged; both read the tree they are run in.

**`entire graph` indexes per directory.** A fresh worktree has no index, so the
first `entire graph search` there pays a full build (~5 s on this repo, measured)
and the symbol ids it returns are namespaced by the directory name
(`local/<branch>:Go:…`). Nothing breaks; do not be surprised by the first search
being slow or by ids that do not match another worktree's.

**Clean up when the PR is merged**, from the main checkout:

```bash
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
git worktree list          # what is still out there
git worktree prune         # after a directory was deleted by hand
```

`git worktree remove` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, which is the
point — look before forcing.

**The main checkout stays on `main` and stays clean.** It is what `git fetch
origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` needs after each merge, and what
every new worktree is cut from.

## Git workflow — pull requests only

**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:

```
! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
```

This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.

**The repository is public since 2026-09-06**, which is what makes GitHub-side
enforcement possible at all: a private repo on a free personal plan answers
`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` on both
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` — that was the prior state, and it is not a
description to trust going forward if the repo ever goes private again. Do not
cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting `"protected":
false` as proof of anything either way: that field only ever reflects legacy
branch protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and it read `false`
on the free-private plan whatever the configuration. Query
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` itself (or `gh ruleset check main`) for the
real answer.

A ruleset named `main-protection` (id `22399372`) now targets `refs/heads/main`
only — deliberately not `entire/checkpoints/v1`, which receives automatic
pushes from the Entire hook and would break if rule-gated. It requires a pull
request (0 approving reviews — solo maintainer, the PR is a record not a review
gate) with the `Lint and build` and `Test` checks from `ci.yml` passing,
blocks force-pushes and branch deletion, and grants no bypass. This closes the
gap the mirror alone left open: the Entire mirror's rejection of a direct push
to `main` was, until now, the *only* protection — a second remote pointing
straight at GitHub would have sailed through (see the warning against adding
one, below). Now GitHub itself refuses that push too.

**The `Entire Gates` check is expected to stay red on this repository.** It is
a PR check from the `entire` app, and its **Approvals** gate fails until another
reviewer approves the trail. That approval cannot arrive: the repository has one
developer, so the gate cannot be green, and no second account or dummy reviewer
should be added to satisfy it. The check is not required by `main-protection`
(GitHub reports the PR as `UNSTABLE` but `MERGEABLE`), so a red `Entire Gates`
alone does not block a merge. Merge once `Lint and build` and `Test` pass. The
Findings, Checks and Up to date gates must stay green: if any of them fails, it
is a real signal, so stop and raise it with the user. Agents (orchestrator,
devops) must not stop to ask for agreement over the Approvals failure alone.
To read the reason:
`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="Entire Gates") | .output.summary'`.

Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
and is forwarded to GitHub.

**Pull requests are GitHub's, not Entire's.** Entire has no merge-request
concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So
the PR steps below are `gh`, and the branch they review is one `origin` carried
to GitHub. `entire review` (labs) runs a multi-agent review against the current
branch and is a pre-merge step, not a substitute for the PR.

```bash
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main   # work happens here
git push -u origin <branch>                     # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch>
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
# then, from the main checkout:
git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see below
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
```

**`-R anthnel/devdesk` is not optional.** `gh` infers the repository from a
remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this
repository point to a known GitHub host"*. The flag names the repo directly.
Do not solve this by adding a GitHub remote — see below.

**After a merge, `origin` can read stale for a minute or two.** The mirror lags
GitHub, so `git fetch origin` right after `gh pr merge` may return the *previous*
`main` — with no error, which is the part that misleads. `gh pr view <n> --json state`
says `MERGED` while `git rev-parse origin/main` still points at the commit before
it. Re-run the fetch a moment later; `gh` is what to trust in the meantime,
because it talks to GitHub directly and needs no remote.

**Do not add a second remote pointing at GitHub to work around that.** The
`main-protection` ruleset (above) would now refuse a direct `git push github
main` too, so it is no longer the *only* defeat of the only protection — but a
direct push still bypasses the mirror, and with it the Entire hook that
records checkpoints and sessions, which is not visible until much later.
`origin` is the only remote, deliberately.

**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.


**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
clean:

```bash
git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> .worktrees/<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
cd .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
git reset --hard origin/main
git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
git worktree remove .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
```

- Cycling `Theme`, covered in the view tests:
  - From `default`, → gives `auto`, `ConfigSavedMsg.ThemeChanged` is true, and `config.Load()` returns `auto`.
  - From `auto`, → gives the next named theme (`opts[idx(auto)+1]`), and the file holds it with no `auto` left.

**Verdict : 1 bloquant, 1 important, 3 non bloquants.** Le commentaire est posté sur la story Plane.

**Vérifications lancées**
- `go build`, `go vet ./...` et `gofmt -l` : propres.
- `go test` passe sur `internal/app`, `ui/theme`, `ui/configuration`, `ui/setup`, `config`, `themes`, `ui/cmdsuggest`, `ui/keymap`, `ui/testutil` et `.`.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/app -run 'Theme|Auto|Background'` : vert.

### Bloquant

**`internal/app/theme_auto.go:181-187` (`settleTheme`) : les vues ne sont pas reconstruites quand la réponse du terminal change la palette.**
- Les vues sont créées dans `newWithSize` (`app.go:319-321`) avec la palette sombre, avant toute réponse.
- Elles gardent des styles capturés à la construction :
  - `datatable.setStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())` (`datatable.go:315`) ;
  - `theme.StyleTextInput` ;
  - `theme.SpinnerStyle()`.
- `applyStyles` ne relit le thème qu'au déplacement du curseur.
- `handleConfigSaved` reconstruit les vues (`configuration.go:61-63`, « every view is rebuilt below anyway »). Le chemin réponse OSC 11 ne le fait pas.
- Scénario : `app.theme: auto` sur un terminal clair. Le fond devient `github-light`, mais les tables, champs et spinners gardent les styles du thème sombre jusqu'à la recréation de la vue (texte clair sur fond clair possible).
- Même cas en session : la sauvegarde construit les vues sur le thème sombre, puis la réponse « light » change la palette sans reconstruction.
- Non reproduit : je suis en lecture seule, le constat vient de la lecture du code. Aucun test ne le couvre : ils vérifient `CurrentThemeName` et le fond de `View()`, pas les styles des vues ni leur reconstruction.
- Correction suggérée : dans `settleTheme`, si le nom résolu change (en pratique : réponse « light »), refaire ce que fait `handleConfigSaved`, soit supprimer les vues sauf :config, appeler `createView(currentView)`, puis `requestResize`.
- Attention : `Init` a déjà été exécuté sur la vue d'origine, donc il faut décider quoi faire de l'`Init` de la vue recréée.
- Test à ajouter : après une réponse « light », une table fraîche a bien les styles clairs.
- Sur le timeout ou une réponse « dark », le thème retombe sur le candidat sombre déjà appliqué, donc pas de reconstruction nécessaire.

### Important

**Documentation périmée (étape 7 pas encore faite ?).** La story exige docs-site.
- `README.md:156-165` et `docs-site/docs/reference/configuration.md:10` disent encore de copier les thèmes à la main (« DevDesk does not install them automatically »).
- `docs-site/docs/how-to/run-the-setup-wizard.md:25` annonce toujours un téléchargement réseau.
- `theme_dark`, `theme_light` et `auto` sont absents de docs-site.
- La phrase prévue pour la Rule 115 dans `tui-theme.md` n'est pas là.
- Les deux fichiers `docs/architecture/*` sont à jour.

### Non bloquants

1. **Critère 7 (nom inconnu) incomplet.** Avec `auto`, seul le candidat utilisé est chargé. Un `theme_light` inconnu sur un terminal sombre n'est jamais signalé. Valider les deux candidats au démarrage serait peu coûteux.
2. **Avertissement en double.**
   - `handleThemeDetectTimeout` jette le `Cmd` d'avertissement (« posté au démarrage »), mais `handleBackgroundColor` renvoie celui de `settleTheme`.
   - Avec un `theme_dark` invalide et une réponse « dark », l'avertissement part deux fois (démarrage, puis réponse).
   - `TestThemeAutoCandidateThatCannotBeUsedGivesDefaultAndOneWarning` ne teste que des candidats clairs.
3. **Changement de contexte :** il ne relance pas `chooseTheme`. C'était déjà le cas pour les thèmes nommés, mais `auto` n'est jamais interrogé après un switch.
4. **Cas limite :** si un utilisateur dépose `auto.json` dans `~/.devdesk/themes`, il est masqué par `withAuto` et `IsAutoTheme`. Négligeable.

### Points demandés

- **Détection une seule fois :** OK. `answer` est mis en cache et `pending` empêche toute relecture. Une réponse tardive est ignorée avec un log INFO.
- **Requête avant le fond (garde `View`) :**
  - Au démarrage, `BackgroundColor` reste nil tant que `pending`, donc aucun OSC 11 n'est écrit avant la requête.
  - En session, le reset OSC 111 est écrit, puis la requête part après 100 ms.
  - Les tests d'octets (`theme_auto_program_test.go`) vérifient l'ordre : requête avant le premier SET, reset avant requête.
  - Dans le renderer Bubble Tea, nil après une valeur posée produit bien `ResetBackgroundColor`.
- **Aucun hex hors `colors.go` :** OK (grep sur les fichiers touchés).
- **Rule 110 :** OK. Les `Cmd` ne capturent que des copies de `gen`. Seul `Update` écrit `themeState`. `sendThemeFacts` s'exécute dans `Update`.
- **Rules 115 / 122 / 128 / 121 / 135 / 129 :** OK.
  - « Theme in use » est un `kindStatic` en texte brut.
  - L'avertissement passe par `PostFooter` (qui ignore le texte vide) au niveau Warn.
  - Les champs Theme / Dark theme / Light theme sont des champs à cycle ←→.
  - Textes et logs en anglais.
- **Générations périmées :**
  - Le cas auto → nommé → auto est correct : une échéance ou un timeout ancien est ignoré.
  - Cas limite négligeable : une réponse déjà en vol de l'ancienne requête peut être prise pour celle de la nouvelle.
- **Fuites de timers :** aucune. Ce sont des `tea.Tick` à usage unique (500 ms ou 100 ms), et un `gen` périmé est ignoré.
- **Disparition de la ligne `Theme loaded:` dans `main.go` :** acceptable. Les échecs sont journalisés (`WARN [theme]`) et la vue config affiche le thème actif. Un `log.Printf("INFO [theme] …")` dans `chooseTheme` rendrait la trace (facultatif).
- **`theme_facts_test.go` :** fichier nouveau, non modifié. Le « resize » est le helper `openConfigView`, qui dimensionne la vue :config parce qu'une vue non dimensionnée ne rend rien. Rien n'est affaibli.
- **Tests changés** :
  - `theme_invalid_test.go` et `terminal_background_test.go` passent de « garde la palette » à « défaut + Warn ». C'est la décision utilisateur et le critère 7, pas un affaiblissement.
  - Les tests setup de téléchargement sont remplacés par « aucun fetch » : cohérent avec les thèmes embarqués.
- **« unknown » pour Theme in use :** correct, mais quasi inatteignable. `r.Name` est vide seulement si `Theme.Name` est vide, et `LoadTheme` le renseigne toujours. La branche reste inoffensive.

**Sécurité :** pas de passage `security-reviewer` nécessaire. Le seul point d'entrée externe est un nom de thème. `readThemeFile` joint `name + ".json"` dans le dossier utilisateur (comportement existant) et l'`embed.FS` refuse les chemins invalides.

**Fichiers lus en détail :**
- `internal/app/theme_auto.go`
- `internal/ui/theme/resolve.go`
- les diffs de `app.go`, `view.go`, `configuration.go`, `command_line.go`, `main.go`, `config.go`, `theme/manager.go`
- `ui/configuration/{fields,model,update,forge}.go`
- `ui/setup/{fields,model}.go`
- `themes/embed.go`
- les docs d'architecture

Les tests ont été lus en survol.

// autoAt builds an auto router (detection pending) starting on view.
func autoAt(t *testing.T, view string) *App {
	t.Helper()
	cfg := autoConfig("auto", "", "")
	cfg.App.DefaultView = view
	a := autoRouter(t, cfg)
	testutil.FastTimers(t, &themeDetectTimeout)
	testutil.FastTimers(t, &themeQueryDelay)
	return a
}

// settlers are the three ways a pending detection ends.

	name string

// (h) switchView during the wait: its Init is the only one of the target view.
func TestSwitchViewDuringTheWaitIsNotInitialisedAgainBySettling(t *testing.T) {
	for _, s := range settlers {
		t.Run(s.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			a := autoAt(t, "status")
			init := appInit(t, a)
			timeout, ok := firstOf[themeDetectTimeoutMsg](init)
			if !ok {
				t.Fatal("setup: Init armed no timeout, auto is not pending")

				t.Fatalf("setup: currentView = %q", a.currentView)

			wantInits(t, "the settling that follows ("+s.name+")", updateMsgs(t, a, s.msg(timeout)), 0)

			a := workspacesAuto(t, "auto")
			testutil.FastTimers(t, &themeDetectTimeout)

			timeout, ok := firstOf[themeDetectTimeoutMsg](init)

				t.Fatal("setup: Init armed no timeout, auto is not pending")

// savedNamed is a save that picks a named theme.
func savedNamed(view string) configuration.ConfigSavedMsg {
	cfg := autoConfig("nord", "", "")
	cfg.App.DefaultView = view
	return configuration.ConfigSavedMsg{Config: cfg, ThemeChanged: true}
}

// (j) a named theme chosen during the wait must not lose the start view's Init.
// The start view is the configuration view, which a save keeps rather than
// rebuilds: its fake counts the Inits it receives.
func TestANamedThemeDuringTheWaitInitialisesTheKeptStartViewOnce(t *testing.T) {
	a := autoAt(t, "configuration")
	if a.currentView != command.ViewConfiguration {
		t.Fatalf("setup: currentView = %q, want configuration", a.currentView)
	}
	fake := &fakeView{}
	a.views[command.ViewConfiguration] = fake
	init := appInit(t, a)
	timeout, ok := firstOf[themeDetectTimeoutMsg](init)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("setup: Init armed no timeout, auto is not pending")
	}
	if fake.inits != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("setup: App.Init ran the start view's Init (%d) while pending", fake.inits)
	}

	updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("configuration"))
	if a.themeDetectionPending() {
		t.Fatal("setup: a named theme left the detection pending")
	}
	if fake.inits != 1 {
		t.Errorf("after the named theme: start view Init ran %d time(s), want 1", fake.inits)
	}

	// Nothing afterwards runs it again: stale timeout, late answer, another
	// named theme, then auto chosen again and answered.
	updateMsgs(t, a, timeout)
	updateMsgs(t, a, tea.BackgroundColorMsg{Color: color.White})
	updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("configuration"))
	cfg := autoConfig("auto", "", "")
	cfg.App.DefaultView = "configuration"
	save := updateMsgs(t, a, configuration.ConfigSavedMsg{Config: cfg, ThemeChanged: true})
	if due, ok := firstOf[themeQueryDueMsg](save); ok {
		updateMsgs(t, a, due)
	}
	updateMsgs(t, a, tea.BackgroundColorMsg{Color: color.Black})
	if fake.inits != 1 {
		t.Errorf("after later theme choices: start view Init ran %d time(s), want still 1", fake.inits)
	}
}

// (k) same loss on a view the save rebuilds: counted through its loading message.
func TestANamedThemeDuringTheWaitInitialisesTheRebuiltStartViewOnce(t *testing.T) {
	a := workspacesAuto(t, "auto")

	init := appInit(t, a)
	timeout, ok := firstOf[themeDetectTimeoutMsg](init)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("setup: Init armed no timeout, auto is not pending")
	}
	wantInits(t, "App.Init", init, 0)
	wantInits(t, "the named theme", updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("workspaces")), 1)
	wantInits(t, "the stale timeout", updateMsgs(t, a, timeout), 0)
	wantInits(t, "a late answer", updateMsgs(t, a, tea.BackgroundColorMsg{Color: color.White}), 0)
	wantInits(t, "another named theme", updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("workspaces")), 0)
}

// runs nothing: the flag, not the save, decides.
func TestANamedThemeWithoutADeferredInitRunsNothing(t *testing.T) {
	a := workspacesAuto(t, "nord")
	wantInits(t, "App.Init", appInit(t, a), 1)
	wantInits(t, "the save", updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("workspaces")), 0)
}

// (h) switchView during the wait: its Init is the only one of the target view.
func TestSwitchViewDuringTheWaitIsNotInitialisedAgainBySettling(t *testing.T) {
	for _, s := range settlers {
		t.Run(s.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			a := autoAt(t, "status")
			init := appInit(t, a)
			timeout, ok := firstOf[themeDetectTimeoutMsg](init)
			if !ok {
				t.Fatal("setup: Init armed no timeout, auto is not pending")
			}
			sw := drain(t, a.switchView(command.ViewWorkspaces))
			wantInits(t, "switchView", sw, 1)
			if a.currentView != command.ViewWorkspaces {
				t.Fatalf("setup: currentView = %q", a.currentView)
			}
			wantInits(t, "the settling that follows ("+s.name+")", updateMsgs(t, a, s.msg(timeout)), 0)
		})
	}
}

// (i) reinitializeViews (context switch) during the wait, same demand.
func TestReinitializeViewsDuringTheWaitIsNotInitialisedAgainBySettling(t *testing.T) {
	for _, s := range settlers {
		t.Run(s.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			a := workspacesAuto(t, "auto")
			testutil.FastTimers(t, &themeDetectTimeout)
			init := appInit(t, a)
			timeout, ok := firstOf[themeDetectTimeoutMsg](init)
			if !ok {
				t.Fatal("setup: Init armed no timeout, auto is not pending")
			}
			wantInits(t, "App.Init", init, 0)
			wantInits(t, "reinitializeViews", drain(t, a.reinitializeViews()), 1)
			wantInits(t, "the settling that follows ("+s.name+")", updateMsgs(t, a, s.msg(timeout)), 0)
		})
	}
}

// savedNamed is a save that picks a named theme.
func savedNamed(view string) configuration.ConfigSavedMsg {
	cfg := autoConfig("nord", "", "")
	cfg.App.DefaultView = view
	return configuration.ConfigSavedMsg{Config: cfg, ThemeChanged: true}
}

// (j) a named theme chosen during the wait must not lose the start view's Init.
// The start view is the configuration view, which a save keeps rather than
// rebuilds: its fake counts the Inits it receives.
func TestANamedThemeDuringTheWaitInitialisesTheKeptStartViewOnce(t *testing.T) {
	a := autoAt(t, "configuration")
	if a.currentView != command.ViewConfiguration {
		t.Fatalf("setup: currentView = %q, want configuration", a.currentView)
	}
	fake := &fakeView{}
	a.views[command.ViewConfiguration] = fake
	init := appInit(t, a)
	timeout, ok := firstOf[themeDetectTimeoutMsg](init)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("setup: Init armed no timeout, auto is not pending")
	}
	if fake.inits != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("setup: App.Init ran the start view's Init (%d) while pending", fake.inits)
	}

	updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("configuration"))
	if a.themeDetectionPending() {
		t.Fatal("setup: a named theme left the detection pending")
	}
	if fake.inits != 1 {
		t.Errorf("after the named theme: start view Init ran %d time(s), want 1", fake.inits)
	}

	// Nothing afterwards runs it again: stale timeout, late answer, another
	// named theme, then auto chosen again and answered.
	updateMsgs(t, a, timeout)
	updateMsgs(t, a, tea.BackgroundColorMsg{Color: color.White})
	updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("configuration"))
	cfg := autoConfig("auto", "", "")
	cfg.App.DefaultView = "configuration"
	save := updateMsgs(t, a, configuration.ConfigSavedMsg{Config: cfg, ThemeChanged: true})
	if due, ok := firstOf[themeQueryDueMsg](save); ok {
		updateMsgs(t, a, due)
	}
	updateMsgs(t, a, tea.BackgroundColorMsg{Color: color.Black})
	if fake.inits != 1 {
		t.Errorf("after later theme choices: start view Init ran %d time(s), want still 1", fake.inits)
	}
}

// (k) same loss on a view the save rebuilds: counted through its loading message.
func TestANamedThemeDuringTheWaitInitialisesTheRebuiltStartViewOnce(t *testing.T) {
	a := workspacesAuto(t, "auto")
	testutil.FastTimers(t, &themeDetectTimeout)
	init := appInit(t, a)
	timeout, ok := firstOf[themeDetectTimeoutMsg](init)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("setup: Init armed no timeout, auto is not pending")
	}
	wantInits(t, "App.Init", init, 0)
	wantInits(t, "the named theme", updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("workspaces")), 1)
	wantInits(t, "the stale timeout", updateMsgs(t, a, timeout), 0)
	wantInits(t, "a late answer", updateMsgs(t, a, tea.BackgroundColorMsg{Color: color.White}), 0)
	wantInits(t, "another named theme", updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("workspaces")), 0)
}

// (l) a named theme saved when no Init was held back (startup was not auto)
// runs nothing: the flag, not the save, decides.
func TestANamedThemeWithoutADeferredInitRunsNothing(t *testing.T) {
	a := workspacesAuto(t, "nord")
	wantInits(t, "App.Init", appInit(t, a), 1)
	wantInits(t, "the save", updateMsgs(t, a, savedNamed("workspaces")), 0)
}

Story

Entrées : docs/ux/bubbletea-v2-improvements.md §2.5 ; .claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md (§2, §4 F6). Module : Migration Go 1.27 et Charm v2.

Compte rendu du tester (rapporté par l'orchestrator, le tester n'avait pas accès à Plane) : `mise run check` exit 0 (fmt, vet, lint 0 issue, tests sans échec), -race ciblé vert ; les 8 critères sont couverts par des tests (octets via io.Pipe pour l'ordre OSC 11 / fond). Depuis, trois tours de correctifs de revue : reconstruction des vues sur changement de palette, Warn pour theme_dark et theme_light sans doublon, Init de la vue de départ différé pendant la détection (drapeau consommé par switchView, reinitializeViews, handleConfigSaved) ; tests ciblés, -race et lint verts. DEVDESK-258 est livrée en PR #367 (https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/367), mais pas mergée : les checks `Lint and build` et `Test` étaient encore en cours au dernier relevé. Je n'ai pas non plus passé la story en Done. J'ai supprimé `.agent-progress/DEVDESK-258.md`.

## Ce qui est fait
- **Thème auto :** `app.theme: auto` utilise deux nouvelles clés, `app.theme_dark` (défaut `default`) et `app.theme_light` (défaut `github-light`). Sans `auto`, rien ne change et le terminal n'est pas interrogé.
- **Détection :**
  - DevDesk interroge le terminal une seule fois (OSC 11).
  - Sans réponse après 500 ms, il retombe sur le thème sombre, sans message.
  - Choisir `auto` en cours de session interroge le terminal s'il n'a pas encore répondu.
- **Thèmes embarqués :** les 12 thèmes de `themes/*.json` sont dans le binaire, et un fichier de `~/.devdesk/themes/` de même nom reste prioritaire.
- **`dk setup` :** il ne télécharge plus rien.
- **Thème refusé :** tout échec de chargement (nom inconnu, JSON illisible, hex invalide) donne le thème par défaut et un avertissement au footer. Un thème personnel utilisé par `auto` doit aussi passer un contraste de 4,5:1.
- **`:config` :** nouveaux champs `Dark theme` et `Light theme`, et une ligne `Theme in use` qui indique le thème effectif et la raison.
- **Docs :** README, docs-site, `docs/architecture`, Rule 115 et la décision D125 dans `docs/backlog.md`. Pas d'ADR.

## Comment c'est vérifié
- **Tester :** `mise run check` à exit 0 (lint à 0 issue, aucun test en échec), `-race` ciblé vert. Les 8 critères de la story sont couverts par des tests, dont l'ordre de la requête OSC 11 et du fond du thème, vérifié sur les octets émis.
- **Après les correctifs de revue :**
  - `go test ./internal/app` complet vert (292 s, rapporté par le coder).
  - Tests ciblés et `-race` verts.
  - Lint à 0 issue.
  - J'ai relancé moi-même les tests ciblés et ceux de `config`, `theme`, `configuration`, `setup` et `themes` : tous verts.
- **Non revu :** le dernier tour de correctifs (drapeau d'`Init` différé) n'a pas eu de revue finale, par ta décision de ne pas en refaire.

## Reste à faire
- **Merge :** attendre `Lint and build` et `Test` verts sur la PR, puis ton accord. `Entire Gates` peut rester rouge sur Approvals seul.
- **Après le merge :**
  - Passer DEVDESK-258 en Done.
  - Passer les 8 tâches de la story, aujourd'hui en In Review, en Done.
  - Charger `release-flow`.
  - Supprimer le worktree.
- **Tests manuels :** terminal clair et sombre, tmux, Windows Terminal et WSL, SSH.
- **Story à ouvrir :** un changement de contexte ne réapplique pas le thème, et `auto` n'est pas réinterrogé après un switch. Ce défaut existait déjà pour les thèmes nommés.

## Risques
- **Premier affichage :** un éclair sombre est possible sur un terminal clair, le temps de la réponse.
- **Retrait d'un thème embarqué :** il casserait les configs qui le nomment, la liste embarquée devenant un contrat.
- **Dépassement du quota de revue :** les correctifs de revue ont dépassé le quota de deux allers-retours. Tu les as acceptés explicitement, dont un dernier tour sur le drapeau d'`Init` différé.

Si une autre story suit, lance `/clear` avant.
